blocks.text: The letters ⁧ي⁩ and ⁧و⁩ have three roles: consonant (y, w)Long vowel (ī, ū) and second element of a diphthong (ay, aw). In this lesson you learn to recognize the role by looking at vocal signs, thus completing the system of vowels of the standard Arabic.

rows: 5–6 hours · one week at a standard pace

blocks.text: Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-02, Anki deck (tag L0-02), telephone to register
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. recognize, pronounce and write ⁧ي⁩ and ⁧و⁩ in all their forms;
2. determine whether ⁧ي⁩ and ⁧و⁩ are consonant, long or diphthong vowel;
3. read and write ī, ū, ay, aw distinguishing them from short vowels;
4. write the conjunction ⁧وَ⁩ together with the following word;
5. read, write and translate the ten words of the vocabulary.
Plan of the week.

blocks.text: 7 Correction · errors in Anki · review

The role of ⁧ي⁩ or ⁧و⁩ you can understand by looking at the vowel of the previous consonant and the sign on the ⁧ي⁩ / ⁧و⁩ It's the same. The rules are three and have no exceptions in the vocalized text.
fatḥa + ⁧و⁩ with sukūn diphthong aw ⁧ثَوْب⁩ ṯawb
Two examples that summarize everything:
• ⁧بُيُوت⁩ buyūt Case: ⁧ب⁩ has ḍamma (bu-), ⁧ي⁩ has ḍamma therefore it is consonant (yū-), ⁧و⁩ no signs after
ḍamma è ū long, ⁧ت⁩ Close. Syllabes: bu-yūt.
• ⁧ثِيَاب⁩ ṯiyāb Clothes: ⁧ث⁩ has kasra, but ⁧ي⁩ has yours fatḥa, so it is not ī long but consonant y. Syllabes: ṯi- yāb, notṯīāb».
1.1 Why it counts: text without vowels

Without vocal signs, ⁧ا و ي⁩ These are your main clues: they mark long vowels and diphthongs, while short vowels disappear. The spelling ⁧بيت⁩ It can only be bayt between the words you know, but generally a ⁧و⁩ or a ⁧ي⁩ without signs leaves more readings open: you will see it with ⁧دين⁩ ( dīn (b) in the case of a contract for the purpose of the contract, the contract shall be signed by the person concerned. L0-03.
1.2 Long vowels really long
As per ā, also ī and ū They last about twice as long as the short ones. bint and bintī (The girl is my daughter) are distinguished only by the ī final: if you shorten it, the possessive disappears.
1.3 Full diphthongs
In Arabic, standard ay and aw are pronounced as two sounds in one syllable: bayt come in ṯawb as "tau" + b. In Egyptian and Levant dialects they often become ē and ō (bēt, tōb): In MSA avoid it.

⁧وَ⁩ wa--and---and writes attached to the word that follows, without space: ⁧وَبِنْت⁩ wa-bint \'e a girlÂ's. As a result ⁧و⁩ It never connects to the left, the next word keeps its initial form: graphically you see a detachment, but it is only one word.
• Consonant sound. /j/, approximate palatal: the back of the tongue approaches the hard palate without Touch it, as in the semi-consonant of
• Long vowel. [iː] after kasra: tīn, bintī.

• Tracked. Initial and median: a tooth equal to that of ⁧ب⁩ , with two points below . Isolated and final: one The curve is in the shape of an upside-down curve that descends below the line, with the two points under the belly.
• Examples ⁧بَيْت⁩ bayt (medial) · ⁧تِين⁩ tīn (medial) ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ baytī (final).
• Typical error. In initial or median position, confuse it with ⁧ب ت ث ن⁩ : is the only one in the group with two dots below.
• Consonant sound. /w/, approximate labiovelar: rounded lips and back of the tongue raised towards the veil, such as the semi-consonant of man and other than man.
• Long vowel. [uː] after ḍamma: tūt, nūn.
• Tracked. A round eyelet that rests on the line, then a tail that descends below the row to the left.
Only two forms: isolated ⁧و⁩ and final ⁧ـو⁩ .
• Does not link to the next letter. It is the second of the six letters "separate" ( ⁧ا و⁩ and, L0-03, ⁧د ذ ر ز⁩ ).
• Examples ⁧ثَوْب⁩ ṯawb (final) · ⁧تُوت⁩ tūt (final: ⁧ت⁩ following isolated restart) · ⁧وَ⁩ wa (isolated).
• Typical error. Read ⁧و⁩ as "M": tūt, not toat: ṯawb, not tob.
2.3 Reading contrasts
Here the minimum lexical pairs are few: trained with series of syllables and words that change only for length.
Diphthong/long vowels ⁧بَيْت⁩ – ⁧بُيُوت⁩ bayt buyūt house • houses

Notes of use. ⁧بَيْت⁩ bayt: Dittongo ay · ⁧بُيُوت⁩ buyūt: ⁧ي⁩ consonant, ⁧و⁩ long vowel · ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ baytī: The suffix -ī is studied in A1-09 · ⁧تِين⁩ tīn: ī long · ⁧تُوت⁩ tūt: ū long · ⁧ثَوْب⁩ ṯawb: Dittongo aw · ⁧ثِيَاب⁩ ṯiyāb: ⁧ي⁩ consonant: ṯi-yāb · ⁧وَ⁩ wa: You write together with the following word: ⁧وَبَيْت⁩ . The suffix -ī Mine, mine ( ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ baytī, ⁧بِنْتِي⁩ bintī) is an anticipation of A1-09: here it is used to read the ī long at the end of your word.

Oral production
1. Diphthongs. Read bayt, ṯawb, bayna ten times each with full diphthong; then pronounces on purpose «bēt» e «tōbTo feel the difference.
2. Length. Alternate bint / bintī and tibn / tīn: The long one lasts twice as long.
3. Consonant y. Read ⁧ثِيَاب⁩ scanning ṯi-yāb, then at normal speed without merging the two vowels.
4. Registration. Register on timed reading and check: full diphthongs, long vowels, ⁧ث⁩ Interdental.
